questions.title: Section A: Multiple Choice, Matching, Terminology and True/False

subQuestions.questionText: A market approach that focuses on a small target segment of the market:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D - Niche (2 marks)
A niche market approach focuses on a small, specific target segment of the market rather than the mass market.

subQuestions.questionText: … in a market divide large shipments of produce to sell them in smaller units.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B - Retailers (2 marks)
Retailers buy produce in bulk and divide it into smaller units to sell to consumers.

subQuestions.questionText: The following is NOT a way to streamline and improve an agribusiness chain:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - Lack of capital (2 marks)
Lack of capital is a problem/limitation, not a way to improve the agribusiness chain.

subQuestions.questionText: The straight line Y in the graph below represents the … a product. (Refer to the graph in the question paper showing a horizontal line Y on axes of price vs quantity.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - demand for (2 marks)
A horizontal line on a price-quantity graph represents perfectly elastic demand for a product.

subQuestions.questionText: A method to improve labour productivity:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D - Better working conditions (2 marks)
Better working conditions improve worker morale and labour productivity.

subQuestions.questionText: The production factor that has a financial value and is a primary natural agricultural resource:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - Land (2 marks)
Land is the primary natural agricultural resource which has financial value.

subQuestions.questionText: ONE of the following is NOT a problem associated with capital:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A - Application of fertilisers (2 marks)
Application of fertilisers is a farming practice, not a problem with capital. The other options (high risk, undercapitalisation, high interest rate) are all problems associated with capital.

subQuestions.questionText:
The Labour Relations Act, 1995 (Act 66 of 1995) deals with the following issues:
(i) Procedures for the resolution of labour disputes
(ii) Prevention of unfair labour practices
(iii) Health and safety of workers
(iv) Social justice and fair working conditions
Choose the CORRECT combination:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B - (i), (ii) and (iv) (2 marks)
The Labour Relations Act deals with resolution of labour disputes, prevention of unfair labour practices, and social justice and fair working conditions. Health and safety falls under the Occupational Health and Safety Act.

subQuestions.questionText: An example of the phenotype in cattle is the …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D - colour of the hair and the presence of horns (2 marks)
Phenotype refers to observable physical traits, such as hair colour and presence of horns.

options.A: total product of the environmental variation.
options.B: sum of the environmental variation and genetic variation.
options.C: total product of the genetic variation.
options.D: colour of the hair and the presence of horns.

subQuestions.questionText: A male animal that has 98 chromosomes will have the following:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B - 48 pairs of autosomes and an XY chromosome (2 marks)
98 chromosomes = 49 pairs total. Subtracting 1 pair of sex chromosomes (XY for male) leaves 48 pairs of autosomes.

options.A: 49 pairs of autosomes and an XY chromosome
options.B: 48 pairs of autosomes and an XY chromosome
options.C: 49 pairs of autosomes and an XX chromosome
options.D: 48 pairs of autosomes and an XX chromosome

subQuestions.questionText: Choose a term from COLUMN B that matches the description in COLUMN A: The path a product follows from the farmer to the consumer. (Options: A. fixed costs, B. genetic modification, C. permanent, D. marketing chain, E. part-time, F. variable costs, G. marketing supply, H. insurance)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D - marketing chain (2 marks)
The marketing chain is the path a product follows from the farmer/producer to the consumer.

subQuestions.questionText: Choose a term from COLUMN B that matches: The costs that depend on production of an enterprise in a farming venture.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: F - variable costs (2 marks)
Variable costs are costs that change/depend on the level of production.

subQuestions.questionText: Choose a term from COLUMN B that matches: A form of risk management where a contract ensures guaranteed compensation for losses.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: H - insurance (2 marks)
Insurance is a contractual risk management tool that compensates for losses.

subQuestions.questionText: Choose a term from COLUMN B that matches: The type of farmworker who works throughout the year.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - permanent (2 marks)
Permanent farmworkers are employed throughout the year.

subQuestions.questionText: Choose a term from COLUMN B that matches: An example of biotechnology.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B - genetic modification (2 marks)
Genetic modification is an example of biotechnology in agriculture.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term: The quantity of products demanded exceeds the quantities offered.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Shortage (2 marks)
A shortage occurs when demand exceeds supply.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term: A legal binding document between the farmer and the farm worker that needs to be signed on employment.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Contract (2 marks)
A contract is the legally binding employment document.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term: A phenotypical expression by which one allele masks the effect of another.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Dominant (2 marks)
Dominance is when one allele masks the expression of another (recessive) allele.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term: A pattern of inheritance in which the expression of one gene is controlled by another gene.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Epistasis (2 marks)
Epistasis is when one gene controls or masks the expression of another gene at a different locus.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term: The transmission of characteristics from parents to offspring.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Heredity (2 marks)
Heredity is the transmission of genetic characteristics from parents to offspring.

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) to make the statement TRUE: A marketing approach that responds to increasing concerns about the environment, is advertising.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Green marketing/eco-labelling (1 mark)
Green marketing (or eco-labelling) is the marketing approach that addresses environmental concerns.

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) to make the statement TRUE: The provision of incentives and recognition of work with rewards to increase labour productivity is referred to as innovation.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Motivation (1 mark)
Motivation refers to providing incentives and rewards to improve productivity.

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) to make the statement TRUE: Mass selection is based on the quality of the animal's ancestors.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Pedigree (1 mark)
Pedigree selection is based on the quality of an animal's ancestors.

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) to make the statement TRUE: Colour-blindness is a sex-linked trait which is characterised by blood-clotting failure.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Haemophilia (1 mark)
Haemophilia is the sex-linked trait characterised by blood-clotting failure (colour-blindness affects vision, not blood clotting).

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) to make the statement TRUE: Atavism is the phenomenon in which a characteristic is determined by various pairs of genes.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Polygenic inheritance (1 mark)
Polygenic inheritance occurs when a characteristic is determined by multiple gene pairs.

subQuestions.questionText: Define the concept marketing.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: The process of planning and executing the conception, pricing, promotion (1 mark)
Mark 2: and distribution of ideas, goods and services to consumers (1 mark)
[Award 2 marks for a complete definition covering both planning/execution and distribution to consumers]

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate for EACH of the descriptions below, (a) to (c), whether it refers to marketing or selling:
(a) Market survey conducted on 300 customers to determine their needs
(b) Focus on acquiring money to buy a container to sell the produce in that season
(c) Focus on the number of bags of potatoes sold at a time
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Marketing (1 mark) - market research is part of marketing
(b) Selling (1 mark) - focus is on transactional/short-term cash flow
(c) Selling (1 mark) - focus on units sold rather than meeting customer needs

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the marketing concept illustrated by demand A and B above. (Refer to diagrams showing demand A: Price R55, 100 bags demanded; demand B: Price R85, 95 bags demanded.)
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Price inelasticity of demand (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason for the answer to QUESTION 2.2.1.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: The demand changed slightly despite the huge change in price (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the reason why consumers responded in such a way to the price change.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Maize meal is a necessity/staple food (1 mark)
Mark 2: people will therefore buy maize meal even with a price increase (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the factor that led to the difference in the number of bags demanded.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Price (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Avocado pear farmers grouped themselves in order to produce and sell their produce together. Identify an agricultural marketing system used by the farmers.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Cooperative marketing (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the role of the marketing system in QUESTION 2.3.1.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Production/selling/marketing (1 mark) - any one accepted

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO benefits of the marketing system in QUESTION 2.3.1 for the farmers.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Lower marketing costs/cost distribution
• Requirements/services are supplied cheaper/bulk purchasing
• More bargaining power
• Access to funding/credit to producers
• Higher prices are obtained
• Elimination of the intermediaries
• Potential for growth
• Access to better infrastructure
• Branding
• Risk sharing
• Farmers spend more time on producing than on marketing
• Access to professional expertise

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO factors that may hamper the marketing of avocado pears.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Perishability/spoilage
• Seasonal fluctuations in production
• Lack of capital
• Poor infrastructure
• Wide distribution of production areas
• Ineffective control over production
• Risk/theft/accidents
• Standardisation
• Large volume in relation to value/bulkiness

subQuestions.questionText: The pictures show the marketing of grapes using specially designed cardboard boxes that have holes on the sides and which are recycled after use. Identify the marketing function illustrated above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Packaging (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State THREE characteristics of the cardboard boxes which make them suitable for marketing grapes.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any THREE of the following (1 mark each):
• Clean/dry/undamaged/suitable for the product
• No foreign tastes/odours
• Free of visible signs of fungal growth
• Strong/rigid/solid
• Recyclable/biodegradable
• Easy to handle
• Identification

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE reason for using cardboard boxes with holes.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer (any 1, 1 mark): Allow air flow / reduce spoilage / health reasons

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE aspect that should be included in EACH of the following components of a business plan:
(a) Title page
(b) Human resource plan
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Title page - any 1 (1 mark): Name of the business/person; Logo; Address; Contact details of the business/person
(b) Human resource plan - any 1 (1 mark): Number and type of employees; Competencies and skills needed

subQuestions.questionText: Name an electronic resource used as a tool for drawing up a business plan.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Computer software programmes (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO reasons for drawing up a business plan.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• To test the feasibility/economic viability of the business idea
• To secure funding
• To determine financial needs/budget
• To guide daily operations/outlines roles and responsibilities
• To allow the entrepreneur to foresee problems
• To reposition/analyse the business
• To gain knowledge about marketing opportunities and competitors
• To ensure effective business management
• Mapping out the objectives/goals of the enterprise
• Provides information on the internal/external business environment
• Provision of time frames

subQuestions.questionText: State ONE problem that could be encountered when drawing up a business plan.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 1 of the following (1 mark):
• Incomplete/with gaps
• Vague
• Unrealistic assumptions/over ambitious
• Hiding weaknesses and risks
• Not taking the competition into account
• Using the incorrect format
• Insufficient research
• Insufficient technical details

subQuestions.questionText:
Rearrange the phases of the entrepreneurial process below in the CORRECT order by writing down only the letters (A to D).
A. Determine the available labour, machinery and equipment.
B. Production and supply of goods.
C. Plan the business to secure funding.
D. Realisation of the absence of suitable products and services.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct order (1 mark each):
1. D (Realisation of the absence of suitable products and services)
2. A (Determine the available labour, machinery and equipment)
3. C (Plan the business to secure funding)
4. B (Production and supply of goods)

subQuestions.questionText:
SWOT analysis is used in a farming enterprise. Indicate TWO aspects of the SWOT analysis that are regarded as:
(a) Internal aspects
(b) External aspects
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Internal aspects (2 marks): Strengths and Weaknesses (1 mark each)
(b) External aspects (2 marks): Opportunities and Threats (1 mark each)

subQuestions.questionText: Match the economic characteristic of land with the statement: The life of soil is unlimited if used correctly. (Options: specific environment; durability; indestructibility; availability; restrictedness)
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Durability (1 mark)
Durability refers to the unlimited life of soil if used correctly.

subQuestions.questionText: Match the economic characteristic of land with the statement: Only 12% of the soil in South Africa can be cultivated.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Availability (1 mark)
Availability refers to the limited percentage of arable soil.

subQuestions.questionText: Match the economic characteristic of land with the statement: Soil may be damaged, but cannot be destroyed.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Indestructibility (1 mark)
Indestructibility means soil can be damaged but not destroyed.

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO economic functions of land.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Land provides space/area
• Provides raw materials
• Provides minerals
• Food security
• Serves as collateral/security

subQuestions.questionText: Government proposed a 5% increase in the minimum wage for farmworkers. Some farmworkers work 10 hours and more per day for six days a week. Researchers have also reported the highest number of new HIV/Aids infections on farms. Name the labour legislation used to address the wage issue in the scenario above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Basic Conditions of Employment Act (Act 75 of 1997)/BCEA (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Identify TWO problems experienced by farmworkers in the scenario above.
subQuestions.memoText:
(1 mark each):
• Long working hours
• HIV/AIDS infections

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO ways in which the impact of HIV/Aids infections on farms could be addressed.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• HIV/AIDS awareness campaigns/education/workshops
• Provisions of condoms
• Nutritional schemes
• Provision of ARVs
• Avoid multiple partners
• Support groups
• Treatment of STIs

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO types of temporary farmworkers based on the terms of employment.
subQuestions.memoText:
(1 mark each):
• Casual worker
• Seasonal worker

subQuestions.questionText: The table shows a record of income and expenses of a farm with three different enterprises (cattle, tomatoes, maize). Calculate the profit or loss of the cattle enterprise from the record of income and expenses above. Show ALL calculations, including the formula. Cattle: Total expenses R13 041; Total income R455 000.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Formula: Profit/loss = total income - total expenditure (1 mark)
Mark 2: Substitution: = R455 000 - R13 041 (1 mark)
Mark 3: Profit = R441 959 (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Compare the tomato and maize enterprises in terms of their profit. (Tomato profit: R132 700; Maize profit: R39 770)
subQuestions.memoText:
Either of the following comparisons (2 marks):
• The profit of tomatoes is higher (1 mark) than that of maize (1 mark)
• The profit of maize is lower (1 mark) than that of tomatoes (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Identify TWO overhead expense items in the income statement above.
subQuestions.memoText:
(1 mark each):
• Fuel
• Truck licence

subQuestions.questionText: A farmer inherited a 20 ha farm with machinery, vehicles, livestock and investments in cash, all worth R20 300 000, and credit of R420 000 for a truck. Identify the TWO types of capital in the scenario above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Fixed (e.g. farm/land)
• Movable (e.g. machinery, vehicles)
• Floating/working/production (e.g. livestock, cash investments)

subQuestions.questionText: Give the total value of the assets in the scenario above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: R20 300 000 (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Deduce the type of credit obtained by the farmer from the scenario above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Medium term credit (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Justify the answer to QUESTION 3.5.3.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: It is used to purchase movable capital/truck (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Name the capital item that is regarded as a liability in the scenario above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Truck (1 mark)
The truck was bought on credit, so the outstanding credit makes it a liability.

subQuestions.questionText:
The table shows agricultural products and the prices in 2010 and 2020:
Yellow maize (R/ton): 2010 = 1 000, 2020 = 2 900
Chicken (c/kg): 2010 = 820, 2020 = 2 400
Wheat (R/ton): 2010 = 2 200, 2020 = 5 400
Beef (c/kg): 2010 = 1 100, 2020 = 6 200
Soy beans (R/ton): 2010 = 2 500, 2020 = 5 700
Lamb (c/kg): 2010 = 1 700, 2020 = 9 200
Pork (c/kg): 2010 = 950, 2020 = 2 600
White maize (R/ton): 2010 = 1 100, 2020 = 3 100
Draw a bar graph to compare the prices of animal products in 2010 with those in 2020.
subQuestions.memoText:
Bar graph showing the prices of animal products (Chicken, Beef, Lamb, Pork) in 2010 and 2020.

MARKING CRITERIA (1 mark each):
• Correct heading (e.g. 'Price of animal products in 2010 and 2020')
• X-axis: Correctly calibrated with label (Products)
• Y-axis: Correctly calibrated with label (Price)
• Correct units (c/kg)
• Bar graph format
• Accuracy of bars

Values to plot:
• Chicken: 2010 = 820 c/kg; 2020 = 2 400 c/kg
• Beef: 2010 = 1 100 c/kg; 2020 = 6 200 c/kg
• Lamb: 2010 = 1 700 c/kg; 2020 = 9 200 c/kg
• Pork: 2010 = 950 c/kg; 2020 = 2 600 c/kg

subQuestions.questionText: Differentiate between internal and external forces that influence a farming business.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Internal forces - Those that have their origin on the farm and can be dealt with on the farm (1 mark)
Mark 2: External forces - Those factors the farmer has no control over (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Define risk sharing as a strategy of management.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: The strategy in which the cost of consequences of a risk (1 mark)
Mark 2: is distributed amongst several stakeholders (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: A dairy farmer divides cows into three groups based on different feeds. The cows are genetically identical and kept under the same conditions. The table shows milk yield per cow per year (litres) and total number of cows in each yield range. Identify in the table the number of cows that produced the highest quantity of milk.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: 6 (1 mark)
The highest milk yield range (9 000-10 999 litres) had 6 cows in Group 2.

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the factor that could have led to the differences in milk yield in the information given above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Feeding/Nutrition (1 mark)
Since the cows are genetically identical and kept under the same conditions, the only differing factor is the feed.

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate whether the cause of the differences in milk production in QUESTION 4.1.2 is genetic or environmental.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Environmental (1 mark)
Feeding is an environmental factor (the cows are genetically identical).

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO genetic causes of variation.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Meiosis/crossing over/recombination of genes
• Fertilisation
• Mutation

subQuestions.questionText: The diagram shows a crossing of a white rose plant (WW) with a red rose plant (RR), which produced F1-offspring with pink flowers (RW). Determine the type of dominance in the diagram above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Incomplete dominance (1 mark)
Neither allele is fully dominant; the heterozygote (RW) shows an intermediate (pink) phenotype.

subQuestions.questionText: Use a Punnett square to determine the genotypes of the F2-generation if the F1-offspring (RW × RW) interbreed.
subQuestions.memoText:
Punnett square (RW × RW):
| Gametes | R  | W  |
|---------|----|----|
| R       | RR | RW |
| W       | RW | WW |

MARKING CRITERIA (1 mark each):
• Correct gametes for parent 1 (R, W)
• Correct gametes for parent 2 (R, W)
• Correct offspring (RR, RW, RW, WW)
• Punnett square with gametes and offspring properly drawn

subQuestions.questionText:
Assume that the F2-generation in QUESTION 4.2.2 produced 700 offspring. Determine the following:
(a) Phenotypic ratio of the F2-generation
(b) Number of pink offspring (Show the calculations.)
(c) Percentage of red offspring
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Phenotypic ratio: 1 red : 2 pink : 1 white (1 mark)

(b) Number of pink offspring (2 marks):
Mark 1: Calculation: $\frac{2}{4} \times 700$ (1 mark)
Mark 2: = 350 pink offspring (1 mark)

(c) Percentage of red offspring: 25% (1 mark)
[$\frac{1}{4} \times 100 = 25\%$]

subQuestions.questionText: A farmer breeds Hereford bulls with traditional Nguni-type cows. The offspring tend to have a higher growth rate and are more resistant to parasites and diseases. Identify the animal breeding system applied in the scenario above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Cross breeding (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason for the answer to QUESTION 4.3.1.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Two different breeds are crossed/Hereford and Nguni (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Deduce TWO characteristics of the offspring in the scenario above that makes them better than the parents.
subQuestions.memoText:
(1 mark each):
• Higher growth rate
• More resistant to pests/parasites/diseases

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO advantages of inbreeding.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Uniform/homozygous offspring are produced
• Farmer obtains pure-bred groups
• Good characteristics from the ancestors are maintained
• Bad recessive genes can be eliminated
• Helps with selection between family groups
• Herd has greater prepotency

subQuestions.questionText:
Below is a pedigree diagram showing the inheritance of disease resistance in goats. R = high disease resistance; r = low disease resistance. Determine whether the following individuals are homozygous or heterozygous:
(a) 4
(b) 5
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) 4 - Homozygous (1 mark)
(b) 5 - Heterozygous (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason for the answer to QUESTION 4.4.1(b).
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: The offspring has the recessive allele from the male parent / Offspring 7 is homozygous recessive because it received one of its recessive alleles from parent 5 (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate the genotypes of the individuals below by referring to the pedigree diagram above:
(a) 2
(b) 7
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) 2 - Rr (1 mark) - heterozygous high disease-resistant female
(b) 7 - rr (1 mark) - homozygous recessive low disease-resistant male

subQuestions.questionText: Mutations may make cells look and function differently from normal cells and are sometimes caused by mutagenic agents. Define the term mutation.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Is a sudden change (1 mark)
Mark 2: in the genetic composition of an organism (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO types of mutagenic agents.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Physical
• Chemical
• Biological

subQuestions.questionText: The diagram represents the genetic modification technique in plants (showing desired genes inserted into tumefaciens DNA, then through stages A, B, C to D). Identify the genetic modification technique illustrated above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Agrobacterium tumefaciens / bacterial carriers (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Label A and D in the diagram.
subQuestions.memoText:
A - Recombinant plasmid (1 mark)
D - Transgenic plant / Genetically modified plant / GMO (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Define the structure represented by D.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: A plant whose DNA has been manipulated through technology (1 mark)
Mark 2: to change its original DNA (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State ONE advantage of genetic modification over traditional methods.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 1 of the following (1 mark):
• It is faster
• More precise
• Not limited to organisms of the same species
